reasoning_checks: Fixed operations/investment and genuinely excess cash are explicit in the wealth theorem. Cash leaves equity exactly once; dividends and fair repurchases preserve each proportional owner’s cash-plus-share claim, with nonseller ownership increases applied to a smaller equity value.

The payout and valuation comparison occurs at one instant; next-year EPS uses a full year after immediate retirement. Actual announcement, entitlement, payment and weighted-average-share dates are not silently identified.

Cash-funded EPS formula deducts foregone cash income before changing shares. The accretion condition Y/N > y*p requires positive Q and remaining shares and is not a value test. The overpriced Portico case raises EPS to 15/14 while continuing owners lose 40.

Mispricing transfers separately value sold and continuing claims using supplied intrinsic value. Gains sum to zero under fixed aggregate value. Proportional participants share both sides; informed unconstrained sellers are not presumed compelled to tender below known fair value.

Personal-tax exercise tracks dividend tax and the basis of sold and remaining shares under invented rules. Immediate liquidation removes hidden terminal tax positions: totals are 90 versus 92, not the event-cash difference 4.4.

Restricted retention is irrevocable, low-return and without liquidity/investment benefits. Its loss uses a compatible certain alternative return, not a risky operating WACC or an unsupported discount on freely withdrawable cash.

Dunlin operating cash is independently reconstructed from gross receipts and payments. Delayed collection and supplier prepayment shift dates while preserving cumulative operating cash of 20. Project receipts are additional and only occur if its indivisible date-1 investment is funded.

Term debt 50 earns interest 2 at each quarter before final principal repayment 10. New date-1 revolver draws earn one quarter of interest at date 2, then all principal is repaid. No facility rollover, unidentified equity or future receipt is invented to cure an earlier shortfall.

Date-1 effective capacity is min(40, 80−50) = 30. The initial payout permission 25, initial cash floor, first-date borrowing limit and second-date debt maturity are separate constraints. Working-capital states imply first-date bounds 43, 18 and 10.

The maximum 10 is a feasibility ceiling, not an optimum. Payout 8 retains 2 additional usable capacity in the combined state. Undrawn headline line and usable covenant headroom differ, and final term principal 40 survives beyond the planning horizon.

The lab’s date-2 payout ceiling solves its continuous monotone piecewise cash equation after full maturity. An independently changed later receipt makes this date bind at payout 5, and payout 6 fails at maturity by 26/25 despite surviving the earlier draw constraint.

Failed investment plans return no compliant closing balance. Canceling the project removes both the cost 30 and later receipt 36; outside equity repair has an explicit gross contribution and fee, while its investor claim prevents treating extra company cash as old-owner value.

Signaling needs incentives and beliefs that make imitation unattractive. Historical executive views are not a causal estimate or a universal present rule. Credit-line monitoring is cited as one mechanism; the Dunlin commitment uses only its supplied fictional terms.

All three worked cases, eight prompts and complete answers, teach-back and delayed check manually matched for assumptions, units, timing, numerical results and interpretation. Open policy answers have explicit criteria and permit other evidence-backed feasible amounts.

limitations: Portico fair/intrinsic values are supplied teaching inputs, not estimated market opportunities. Off-fair execution is hypothetical and does not establish that informed sellers will transact.
All taxes, dates, credit commitments, covenant rules and cash buffers are invented for the cases; no current jurisdictional treatment, legal payout permission or financing approval is asserted.

The small two-quarter treasury model covers three supplied timing scenarios, synchronized payment batches, an indivisible project, one debt cap and a maturing revolver. It is not a general treasury, liquidity-risk or bankruptcy engine.
A scenario-feasible maximum does not estimate probabilities, an optimal risk policy, whole-firm value or intraperiod liquidity. Additional evidence can change the constraints and decision.

Emergency equity in exercise 7 establishes minimum cash funding only. Valuing ownership dilution and total owner welfare requires separately priced new claims; higher closing cash alone is insufficient.

Author/agent review is not independent human certification or a guarantee of error-free work. Coordinator owns sequential acceptance, integration and publication; browser/mobile/print QA remains separate.
